𝗔𝗨𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗟𝗜𝗔𝗡 𝗣𝗢𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗘 𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗘𝗚𝗘𝗗𝗟𝗬 𝗔𝗦𝗞 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗦𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗘𝗧𝗘 𝗣𝗢𝗦𝗧 𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗝𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗜𝗦𝗜𝗦 𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘𝗦
⁣⁣⁣
𝗔𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗶𝘀𝘁 𝗗𝗿𝗲𝘄 𝗣𝗮𝘃𝗹𝗼𝘂 𝘀𝗮𝘆𝘀 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗱 𝗵𝗶𝗺 𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝟮𝟴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗮 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝘁 — 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗯𝗿𝗼𝗸𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗮𝘄, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝘁 𝗴𝗼𝗻𝗲.
⁣⁣⁣
Let that sink in.
⁣⁣⁣
According to Pavlou, when he asked what law he violated, police admitted he hadn’t broken any. They still wanted the post deleted.
⁣⁣⁣
What was the post?
⁣⁣⁣
Pavlou criticized journalist Craig Hill for claiming the Bondi Beach terror attack was 𝘯𝘰𝘵 anti-Jewish — arguing instead that it was merely opposition to Israeli policy.
⁣⁣⁣
That attack kllled 15 people during a Hanukkah gathering.
⁣⁣⁣
Authorities confirmed it was 𝗜𝗦𝗜𝗦-𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗱.
⁣⁣⁣
Homemade ISIS flags were found in the shooter’s car. The attackers had traveled to the Philippines beforehand. The surviving shooter was charged with 59 offenses, including terrorism.
⁣⁣⁣
Craig Hill’s claim — that this was about 𝘡𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘱𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘪𝘦𝘴 rather than Jewish victims — sparked outrage.
⁣⁣⁣
Pavlou called that framing what it was: laundering jihadist violence through political wordplay.
⁣⁣⁣
That’s when police allegedly called.
⁣⁣⁣
Here’s where it gets darker.
⁣⁣⁣
The shooter, Naveed Akram, worshipped at the Al Madina Dawah Centre in Bankstown — led by radical preacher Wissam Haddad.
⁣⁣⁣
Haddad was later found to have violated Australia’s racial hatred laws in 2025.
⁣⁣⁣
Pavlou had been warning about Haddad for two years before the attack.
⁣⁣⁣
Those warnings? Ignored.
⁣⁣⁣
But criticism after the attack? That gets a police phone call.
⁣⁣⁣
Pavlou says this proves 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗲𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 — and intimidation.
⁣⁣⁣
He has receipts.
⁣⁣⁣
His track record includes:
– Suspension from the University of Queensland
– Multiple arrests for anti-CCP protests
– 23-hour detention in London over a fabricated bomb threat
– Removal from Australian Parliament as a 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘢𝘤𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘴𝘵
– A $10,000 fine for holding protest signs
⁣⁣⁣
In other words: a guy the system already dislikes.
⁣⁣⁣
So let’s connect the dots.
⁣⁣⁣
An activist warns about a radical preacher. Authorities do nothing.
⁣⁣⁣
A follower of that preacher carries out an ISIS-inspired terror attack.
⁣⁣⁣
A journalist downplays the ideology behind it. The activist calls that out.
⁣⁣⁣
And that is what triggers police intervention.
⁣⁣⁣
This isn’t about safety.
⁣⁣⁣
This is about 𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹.
⁣⁣⁣
And when police start asking people to delete lawful speech — while admitting no law was broken — that’s not policing. That’s pressure.
